title: Polymer clay ocean drop earrings
subtitle: Layered blue-and-white teardrop earrings imitating sea and surf
excerpt: Teardrop earrings layered with navy, turquoise, and white polymer clay to suggest ocean waves breaking on shore. The colours are blended at the edges rather than kept crisp, giving an organic watercolour effect. No kiln is required: the earrings cure in a domestic oven at 130°C.
sourceNotes: Technique derived from first principles. Polymer clay earring methods are a widely documented craft technique.

glossaryTerms.definition: A PVC-based modelling material that cures hard in a domestic oven at 110 to 130°C
A polymer clay technique for creating smooth colour gradients by folding two colours of clay together in a repeated pattern

content.text: These earrings layer three ocean-toned
polymer clay
colours in a teardrop drop. White at the top fades into turquoise into navy at the pointed base, suggesting a wave breaking on a sky-blue sea. A basic
Skinner blend
gives a smooth gradient across the teardrop face. No kiln is required.

tools.name: Pottery rolling pin or acrylic roller
Fettling knife or teardrop shape cutter

content.text: Building the gradient
Condition all three colours separately. Roll each into a log about 8 cm long.
Press the three logs side by side in the order: white, turquoise, navy. Press them flat into a slab using the rolling pin.
Fold the slab from one end to the other so the colours line up. Roll flat again. Repeat this fold-and-roll sequence 10 to 12 times until the transitions between colours are smooth.
Cutting and piercing
Roll the gradient slab to 4 mm thick. The white area should sit at the top and navy at the bottom.
Cut two matching teardrop shapes about 3.5 cm tall and 2 cm wide at the widest point, with the point at the base and the flat curve at the top.
Pierce a clean hole at the top of each teardrop with the needle tool, about 3 mm from the edge. The hole must be at least 2 mm in diameter so the jump ring passes through after curing.
Curing
Lay the earrings flat on a ceramic tile and cure at 130°C for 20 minutes. Ventilate the kitchen. Cool fully before handling.
Finishing

The surface will be smooth and slightly matte. Sand with 800-grit sandpaper under water for a stone-like finish, or leave the surface as cured for a softer look. Thread jump rings through the holes and attach earring hooks.
Use and care
Cured polymer clay earrings are lightweight and durable. Remove before swimming or showering. Wipe with a dry cloth.
Variations
Use sandy ochre, terracotta, and deep sienna tones for a desert sunset palette. Cut a round or rectangle shape instead of a teardrop.
Troubleshooter

items.problem: The colour gradient has visible stripes rather than a smooth blend
items.fix: Continue folding and rolling until the colour boundary is fully smooth. 15 to 20 cycles is typical for a very clean blend

items.cause: The hole was too small or the clay around it was too soft
items.fix: Re-pierce after curing with a hand drill or the tip of a nail. Reheat at 130°C for 5 minutes to ensure the area is fully cured after re-piercing
